title: Steady QPS shaping + warm-pool memory reclamation for embeddings router
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: The embeddings router occasionally experiences sharp QPS spikes from bursty tenants and large-batch clients. These spikes lead to long tail latency increases and inefficient warm-pool utilization: we either over-provision GPU memory to keep many warm contexts, or under-provision and pay high cold-init latency costs. Current autoscaling reacts to aggregated queue depth which amplifies oscillation and causes noisy scaling for embeddings endpoints.

Goal: Implement a steady QPS shaping layer combined with a controlled warm-pool memory reclamation policy to smooth incoming demand, reduce cold-starts, and improve median and p99 latencies under bursty load while keeping reserved capacity lower. Provide per-tenant soft-QPS limits, a burst-credit mechanism, and a reclaim policy for idle KV caches/contexts. Ship an operator-safe rollout and monitoring dashboard.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- 30-50% reduction in p99 latency for embeddings during burst windows (measured across top 20 tenants)
- 15-25% reduction in average reserved warm-pool memory footprint across clusters at steady state
- No more than 5% increase in 99th percentile request rejection rate during stress tests (when soft limits enforced)
- Autoscaling events (scale-ups/downs) smoothing: reduce thrashing by 40% vs baseline

Scope: router-level (edge) QPS shaping, per-tenant soft limits, burst-credit accrual and depletion, warm-pool memory reclamation policy on nodes, metrics+alerts, rollout plan, and a small compatibility shim for Dedicated (reserved pools). Not in scope: model re-quantization or kernel-level optimizations.

Risks: incorrect shaping parameters could unfairly penalize high-priority customers; overly aggressive reclamation may cause cache churn and latency spikes; interactions with Dedicated autoscaler need a compatibility layer to avoid double-throttling.
acceptance_criteria: Router applies per-tenant soft QPS limits with observable token bucket state in traces/metrics
Burst-credit mechanism allows short bursts up to configured multiplier and decays predictably
Warm-pool reclaim frees idle KV/cache contexts based on last-access and memory pressure without exceeding p99 latency budget
Dashboard shows QPS shaping utilization, warmed context counts, and reclaimed memory by cluster
E2E stress test demonstrating p99 improvement and reduced autoscale thrash compared to baseline
Runbook updated with rollback steps and customer-visible throttling messaging
implementation_steps: Design shaping algorithm: per-tenant leaky-bucket + global soft-floor; define default parameters and overrides
Implement burst-credit ledger per-tenant with accrual rules and decay window
Expose shaping decisions to tracing and metrics (tags for shaped vs unshaped requests)
Add warm-pool reclamation controller on node agent: LRU by last-access with memory-pressure thresholds
Integrate shaping with existing autoscaler: shaping signals feed autoscaler health, and autoscaler respects shaping headroom
Add feature flag and Dedicated compatibility shim to disable shaping where tenants opted for raw reserved throughput
Create load tests simulating tenant bursts, large-batch clients, and long-tail traffic; baseline comparison harness
Instrument dashboards, alerts, and SLO checks; prepare post-deploy validation queries
tradeoffs: We intentionally prefer soft shaping + burst credits rather than hard rejects to preserve UX; this means occasional backpressure instead of immediate failure. Warm-pool reclamation trades lower steady-state memory for slightly higher cold-init probability; parameters must be tuned. We avoid moving shaping into the runtime to keep router changes lightweight, at the cost of an additional hop in shaping decision-making.
monitoring_signals: primary: p50/p95/p99 request latency for embeddings; shaping_throttled_requests_ratio; burst_credit_balance distribution by tenant; warmed_contexts_per_node; reclaimed_memory_bytes; autoscaler_scale_events_per_minute; queue_depth_post_shape. Secondary: customer error rates, RLUs per tenant. Set alerts for p99 latency regressions >10% from baseline and reclaimed_memory causing >5% cold-starts over a minute.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature-flag in staging with simulated tenant burst traffic and validate metrics. 2) Canary to 5% of production traffic (non-enterprise tenants) for 24h; monitor dashboards and SLOs. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% over 48h if no regressions; collect tenant-level feedback. 4) Target full roll by 2 weeks with fallback flag to disable shaping globally per-region. For Dedicated customers, coordinate with sales/solutions to enable only after compatibility checks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for shaping ledger and burst-credit logic
Integration tests for router+autoscaler interaction using synthetic drivers
Chaos test: simulate memory pressure on nodes and validate warm-pool reclaim behavior
Load test: multi-tenant workload with skewed head tenants and large-batch clients; compare latency and memory metrics to baseline
Canary validation checklist with threshold gates for p99 and error rate
updates: 2026-03-01: Kickoff sync with Infra and Runtime teams. Agreed to keep shaping at router edge and feed signals to autoscaler. Action: Aisha to prototype burst-credit ledger.

2026-03-03: Prototype implemented in router service (branch: feat/emb-qps-shape). Local load test shows smoothed QPS traces and 20% p99 improvement for synthetic bursts. Observability hooks added but not persisted.
2026-03-05: Design review with PM/Evaluations. PM requested per-tenant override via Console with audit log. Added requirement to surface credits in Console UI later (PM follow-up ticket).

2026-03-07: Warm-pool reclaim algorithm options discussed: LRU vs access-frequency. Decided to use last-access LRU with preferential protection for tenants with active burst credits. Infra to implement node-agent reclaim hook.

2026-03-09: Integration test run against autoscaler sandbox. Observed initial thrash when autoscaler reacted to pre-shaping queue depth; fixed by switching autoscaler input to post-shape queue metric. Patch PR opened: GH#4512.
2026-03-10: Prepared canary checklist and dashboard tiles. Security reviewed feature flag scope and recommended audit hooks for per-tenant disables. Scheduling canary for 2026-03-12.
